rows.label: portmanteau
rows.description: word blending the sounds and combining the meanings of two or more others (e.g. smoke + fog → smog)
rows.hook: fuses two terms into one new one, as in brunch from breakfast and lunch

rows.label: onomatopoeia
rows.description: words that imitate the sound they describe
rows.hook: copies the noise of a thing in its name, as with buzz, sizzle and boom

rows.label: fourth wall
rows.description: imaginary vertical plane at the front of a theatrical stage separating performers from the audience
rows.hook: is the invisible barrier a character breaks by speaking straight to the audience

rows.label: Chekhov's gun
rows.description: dramatic principle that every element in a story must be necessary, and irrelevant elements should be removed
rows.hook: says a weapon shown early in a story must be used before the end

rows.label: synecdoche
rows.description: use of a term for a part of something to refer to the whole or vice versa
rows.hook: lets a small piece stand for the whole, as when hands means workers

rows.label: red herring
rows.description: fallacious approach to mislead an audience
rows.hook: is a misleading clue that sends the reader after the wrong culprit in a mystery

rows.label: double entendre
rows.description: wording that is devised to be understood in two ways
rows.hook: is a phrase with two readings, one of them usually cheeky

rows.label: metonymy
rows.description: figure of speech where a thing or concept is referred to indirectly by the name of something closely associated with it
rows.hook: swaps in a closely linked name, as when the crown means the monarchy

rows.label: allegory
rows.description: narrative, whether in prose or verse, in which a character, place or event is used to deliver a broader message about real-world issues and occurrences
rows.hook: uses characters and events as symbols for a deeper lesson, as in Animal Farm

rows.label: malapropism
rows.description: use of an incorrect word in place of a word with a similar sound, resulting in a nonsensical, often humorous utterance
rows.hook: is a comic mix-up of similar-sounding terms

rows.label: unreliable narrator
rows.description: narrator whose credibility has been seriously compromised
rows.hook: tells a story whose teller cannot be fully trusted, as in Gone Girl

rows.label: metaphor
rows.description: figure of speech in which one thing is asserted to be another when it is in fact not so, based on properties of the latter that apply to the former, pointing to similarity
rows.hook: says one thing is another, as in the claim that all the world is a stage

rows.label: euphemism
rows.description: innocuous word or expression used in place of one that may be found offensive or which the speaker wants to hide
rows.hook: softens something unpleasant, as when saying passed away instead of died

rows.label: stream of consciousness
rows.description: narrative device used in literature
rows.hook: pours a character's raw flowing thoughts onto the page, famously in Ulysses

rows.label: in medias res
rows.description: narrative that opens mid-plot, or 'in the middle of things'
rows.hook: begins a tale in the thick of the action, as the Iliad and Odyssey do

rows.label: spoonerism
rows.description: phrase with sounds swapped between words, often intentionally for humor
rows.hook: swaps the starting sounds of two terms, as in saying a well-boiled icicle

rows.label: irony
rows.description: rhetorical device, literary technique, or situation in which there is an incongruity between the literal and the implied meaning
rows.hook: is when the outcome is the opposite of what was expected, as in a fire station burning down

rows.label: idiom
rows.description: combination of words whose meaning cannot be understood by combining the meaning of the component words
rows.hook: is a fixed saying like kicking the bucket, not to be taken literally

rows.label: hyperbole
rows.description: exaggeration as rhetorical device
rows.hook: stretches the truth for effect, as in saying you have told someone a million times

rows.label: oxymoron
rows.description: rhetorical device that uses an ostensible self-contradiction to illustrate a rhetorical point or to reveal a paradox
rows.hook: pairs contradictory terms, as in deafening silence or jumbo shrimp
